claim_register.claim: The product-template agreement places trade and cashflow stamping in a central service. It links their results but explicitly rejects cashflow inheritance from trade stamping. CDUPS queries the latest cashflow result for fixing notices and calls again for trade events. Refresh and adhoc changes are not published to CDUPS in the listed subitems. The preceding notification wording remains ambiguous. No precedence over other SSI designs is established.

claim_register.claim: The request requires nonnull string fields for trackingId, tradeId, majorVersion, asOf, effective, requestDate, bookingEntityFmId, counterpartyFmId, cfiCode, settlementMethod and settlementType. Mapped trade fields carry key and value; their pair validates the request. Trade_Id links records. The legs array requires currency and payerPartyReference. settlementType is hardcoded Cash. The response returns nonnull per-leg currency, payerPartyReference, Vostro and Nostro results. Vostro outcomes are SUCCESS, MULTI_VOSTRO_ERROR and MISSING_VOSTRO_ERROR. Nostro adds DEFAULT_NOSTRO and MULTI_NOSTRO_ERROR. HTTP200 includes Success/default Nostro;400 covers validation or missing trade.500/internal errors and timeouts require at least three retries, three minutes apart, retaining trade ID and major version. No populated sample identifiers are retained.

claim_register.claim: The compatibility proposal targets local-currency utilization for SA, NP and EG, configurable for later entities. Group enrichment requires a supported FX spot/forward/swap taxonomy and exactly two payment currencies. Otherwise, do not enrich the pair. With one Vostro, FXBRREC plus an existing currency pair queries Nostro using that pair; otherwise follow China logic. Missing/multiple Vostro uses primary Nostro with the pair when present. The proposal compares group enrichment against an SSI-service TDS3 query. Missing legs, pair errors, missing Nostro fallback and replay exceptions remain open. The TDS3 option is source-described as slower; no measured performance evidence exists.

claim_register.claim: Trade stamping first queries Vostro, then uses its settlement means/account for Nostro. A blank query falls back to default Nostro; absent Vostro uses legal entity plus currency. The main non-UK sequence tries CFI granularity of first three characters, first two, then second character only. It next ranks country-primary, global-primary, country-secondary, global-secondary. The UK London/SSTL sequence instead selects branch before CFI and primary preference. It drops global candidates when branch-specific candidates exist. Query predicates include branch/global, currency, CFI hierarchy, counterparty, debit/credit, CASH settlement type, settlement-method/FEDWIRE alternatives, and Active/New/Update statuses. A26June2026 note changes CFI_Code to Financial_Instrument_Code. Populated examples do not define universal configuration.

claim_register.claim: The main flow says missing/multiple Vostro plus missing Nostro uses Please advise for both parties. Its good-Vostro/missing-Nostro row enriches PartyA but leaves PartyB as Please advise. The Egypt response table instead enriches PartyB and leaves PartyA To Be Advise for unique Vostro with missing/multiple Nostro. With default Nostro and absent/multiple Vostro, Egypt enriches PartyA and leaves PartyB Please advise. A unique Nostro/Vostro pair enriches both. Buy-side missing/multiple Nostro is blank/To Be Advise; unique Nostro enriches PartyA. These conflicting sell-side outputs require owner resolution; no current party mapping is selected.

claim_register.claim: The Egypt design exposes POST trade enrichment with tracking ID, trade ID, product type and base64 trade SCBML. Single-leg versus near/far-leg results depend on product. Its HTTP200 codes distinguish unique pay/receive stamping;400 identifies missing/default-Nostro, invalid-data and undefined-scenario outputs;500 identifies stamping I/O errors. Per-result values include SUCCESS, missing/multiple Vostro/Nostro and DEFAULT_NOSTRO. It marks notification events out of scope and XML attribute definitions open. Currency plus MAIN is its source-labeled default-Nostro resolution. This is a separate interface design, not a replacement CDUPS contract.

claim_register.claim: Missing Vostro on pay, multiple Vostro on pay/receive, and account mismatch require maker/checker correction. Primary Nostro is displayed; forms validate and compare account/means. A unique secondary Vostro creates a checker-only exception; rejection returns to maker with AdhocSI. Receive with missing Vostro and primary Nostro has no SSI exception. Good stamping can enter adhoc through maker action or checker rejection. Adhoc requires dual-blind matching; pay validates both Vostro/Nostro, receive validates only Nostro. Missing-Nostro handling distinguishes pay from receive and missing from unique Vostro. In the receive/missing-Vostro path, no account/means comparison is required. Source wording for Multi Nostro and blank/form behavior remains inconsistent with later tables.

claim_register.claim: Missing or multiple values start blank. The same maker/checker sees their prior submission/rejection values; a different user sees initial values. Vostro-related exceptions make Vostro editable by default. Nostro-related exceptions make Nostro selectable by default. Mismatch/adhoc starts with Vostro editable and Nostro selectable only through Edit. The detailed table contains conflicting good-stamping Edit-button rows and incomplete Secondary/Adhoc cells. Preserve those gaps rather than inventing a complete editability matrix.

claim_register.claim: The proposal adds Start_EffectiveDate, End_EffectiveDate and Core_EffectiveDate. An end-dated old SSI retains its ID; its replacement uses an _ED suffix. The source proposes deleting the old SSI at the replacement start date, without a new start-date notification. First queries and Vostro exception candidates apply date filtering. An SSI+ update identifies impacted cashflows and retriggers stamping. The pseudocode first accepts end-dated SSI when VD<=end, otherwise rejects it; only then considers start date and VD>=start. It repeats Start_EffectiveDate in its blank-date branch. Both-bound handling, timezone, deletion and refresh completeness remain unresolved. These are proposed storage/filter semantics, not verified source behavior.
